q: How do I calculate the emissions of a pottery kiln firing?
title: Pottery kiln emissions per firing
short: For an electric kiln, multiply the kWh per firing, from a meter or the controller log, by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. For a gas kiln, multiply the LPG or PNG used by its default factor. Divide by the pieces in the load for a per-piece figure.
audience: Studio potters, craft units and small terracotta and stoneware makers

ul: Electric kiln: a plug-in or sub-meter, or rated power times firing hours as an estimate.
Gas kiln: cylinder weight before and after, or the gas meter.
Wood kiln: wood weight, whose CO2 is biogenic and reported separately.

p: Work fired twice, biscuit then glaze, carries both firings. Spread each firing over the pieces it held.
A kiln uses much the same energy to reach temperature whether it is full or half empty, so packing it fully spreads that energy over more pieces.

example.title: Worked example: one glaze firing (illustrative inputs)
lines: Electric kiln: 18 kWh per firing x 0.710 = 12.78 kg CO2
LPG kiln instead: 9 kg LPG x 2.98 = 26.82 kg CO2, 0.670 kg per piece
example.note: Energy per firing is illustrative; read your meter or weigh your cylinder.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
